Place-name differences after replacing the reverse_geocoder 1.5.1 wheel CSV
with the GeoNames cities1000 extract retrieved on 2026-10-26.

The wheel file is 7,851,524 bytes and has no dump date. The dated extract
formats to 9,900,190 bytes and 171,654 rows. Both queries use reverse_geocoder
mode 1 (single-process nearest row) after restoring np.float64 for NumPy 2.

Named coordinates:

- Munich (48.137154, 11.576124): Munich, Bavaria, Upper Bavaria, DE. Unchanged.
- New York (40.7128, -74.0060): New York City, New York, US. Unchanged.
- San Francisco (37.78674, -122.39222): was San Francisco, California, San Francisco County, US. Now Chinatown, California, City and County of San Francisco, US.
- London (51.5214588, -0.1729636): was Bayswater, England, Greater London, GB. Now Church Street, England, Greater London, GB.
- Tokyo (35.6762, 139.6503): was Tokyo, Tokyo, JP. Now Eifuku, Tokyo, Suginami-ku, JP.
- Sydney (-33.8688, 151.2093): was Sydney, New South Wales, City of Sydney, AU. Now Sydney, New South Wales, AU. The admin2 field is empty in the new row.
- Reykjavik (64.1466, -21.9426): was Kopavogur, Capital Region, IS. Now Kopavogur, Capital Region, Kopavogsbaer, IS.
- (0, 0): still Takoradi, Western, GH. The new row adds admin2 Secondi Takoradi.

A sample of 200 coordinates taken from the wheel CSV changed on 108 rows.
Most changes are a closer populated place in the newer dump, or a filled-in
admin2 name. Offline lookup still returns the nearest row. It does not return
the same row as the undated wheel file for every coordinate.

Before this change, lookup_offline read attributes off the CSV dict and called
np.float. On NumPy 2.5.1 both fail, and the exception handler returned no place.
The dated file is what the application now searches.
